welcome.s1Body: This app tracks Unturned servers straight from your PC: who is online, how long each player has played, a map with markers, and an overlay for use with the game running. None of it depends on a third-party site.
welcome.s2Body: With the game folder located, the app reads the maps and detects on its own which server you joined. Without it everything still works, just no maps and no auto-detection.
welcome.s3Body: You can change all of this later in Settings.
welcome.s4Body: Paste an IP:port or a BattleMetrics ID. If the game is open, the app already suggests the server you are on.
welcome.s4Hint: You can also do this later from the menu.

news.n3Body: You can now write notes and paste screenshots on each server and on each map point. It all goes into the backup, and the map learned to read location names and airdrops straight from the game.
news.n2Body: Connect your account to see which servers your friends are on. The overlay gained configurable color, size and transparency, plus global hotkeys and a player-join notification.
news.n1Body: The app now reads the game’s Client.log: it detects which server you joined, suggests the IP when adding one, and shows the live log with filters.

news.n4Body: The app now reads the game's own file (Environment/Nodes.dat) and extracts location names and airdrop points. Coordinates were checked against recognizable landmarks, 1 pixel = 1 meter. The map also got fullscreen, bigger buttons, and a marker card with cover photo and notes.
news.n5Title: Teams: hierarchy, chat, voice and media
news.n5Body: Teams with five roles (owner, admin, moderator, member and guest) and a single rule: you act on whoever is below you. Invites now need a code AND a password, and the password is shown only once. There's channel chat, photo and video sharing, and voice with push-to-talk. It all works on your machine already, hosting the server is what connects people.
news.n6Body: Set the server's wipe and the app counts down on the card, changes color as it gets close, and warns you at the times you pick. It supports repeats (every N days, weekly or monthly), day 31 falls on the last day of shorter months, and the time doesn't drift on daylight saving. After the wipe passes, the card says "was 3h ago" instead of jumping straight to the next one.
news.n7Title: The app tells you where things are
news.n7Body: Hover the map and see the coordinate and the place: "in Novosibirsk", "near Volk" or "3662 m northeast". New markers are pre-named with the location, and team positions show the place before the X/Z. The game's official locations now have locked names, for your own name at the same spot, use "Create mine here".
news.n8Body: On first launch the app follows your Windows language. Switching servers no longer leaves the previous map on screen, every dialog got an in the corner (the only exit used to be at the bottom, off-screen on smaller displays), Esc leaves the server, and the side menu shows whether the overlay is on.

raid.help: The numbers come from the Unturned files on your own machine, the same ones the game reads, so they match your version and the server's mods. The rule is the official one: high armour takes half damage, an “explosion-proof” target only falls to direct damage, and a target that isn't “vulnerable” needs a strong weapon. When two tools do the job in the same number of units, the app suggests the weaker one, so your charges stay for what only they can open.

news.n10Title: The X is now your call
news.n10Body: In Settings, under General, there is an option to keep tracking running when you close the window. Turned on, the app sits next to the clock (in the Windows hidden icons) and keeps following the server; hover the icon to see which one, and how many players. To quit for good, right-click the icon and choose Quit. It ships off: the X closes everything, as it always did.
news.n9Title: The marker lands where you click
news.n9Body: On screens with Windows scaling at 125% or 150%, the marker showed up offset, and the error grew as you panned the map. Two different pixel units were being added as if they were the same. Fixed: at 150% the drift reached 264 pixels and is now zero. The team layer on the map had the same problem.

notes.fichaPlayerPh: Name as it shows in the server list
notes.fichaPlayerHelp: The server only returns the name — there is no SteamID in the player list. That's why the dossier matches by name; if the person renames, just edit this.
notes.fichaNeedPlayer: A dossier has to say who it's about. Type the player's name.
notes.raidEmpty: Set the target and tools in the Raid tab, then click "Pull from calculator".
notes.raidNoPlan: No plan set up in the Raid tab. Pick the target and amount there first.
notes.linksHelp: Linking two notes draws the line between them on the investigation board. Two dossiers linked as allies or team also show up connected in the server's player list.
notes.linksEmpty: No links. Link two dossiers as allies and the player list starts drawing the line between the two names.
notes.linksSaveFirst: Save the note first. You can only link what already exists.
notes.linkNoOthers: There's no other note here to link to.
board.title: Investigation board
board.help: Every note on this server as a card, connected by the links you created. Drag to arrange: the position is saved. The chain button links two cards — click it on one card, then on the other.
board.emptyHow: Create notes and dossiers in the Notes tab. They show up here, and linking two draws the line between them.
board.hint: Drag to arrange. The chain links two cards.
board.tidyAsk: Put every card back on the grid? The current arrangement is lost.
board.pickOther: Now click the chain on the other card.
board.unlinkAsk: These two are already linked. Unlink?
team.newsNeedTitle: A post needs a title — that is what shows in the list.
fichas.teamDossier: Team {team} has a dossier on this person
fichas.noDossier: No dossier. A dossier holds photos, long text and the links that show up in the list.
notes.fichaPhotoHelp: Same rule as the team photo: it is a web address, http and https only. With no link, the icon below is used.
team.deleteType: Type the team name to confirm
team.deleteBodyLocal: This deletes the team and everything shared in it: notes, dossiers, plans, markers and the chat. There is no undo.
team.deleteBodyLive: This deletes the team for everyone. On the server the deletion is held for 24 hours before it is wiped — you can undo within that window.
team.deleteNameMismatch: The name doesn't match. The team was not deleted.
team.deleteScheduled: Team deleted. The server wipes everything in 24 hours — you can undo until then.
team.restored: Deletion undone. The team is back.
team.mapPickServer: Pick one of the team servers in the selector above.
team.mapNoImage: This map hasn't been imported yet. Settings → Import maps from the game.
team.markHelp: In game, /pos shows your position. X and Z are the first and third numbers; Y is height and does not go here.
team.markNeedXZ: A marker needs X and Z. Without coordinates it never shows on the map.
team.markClickMap: Click the map where the spot is.
team.mediaNeedsDeploy: Sending photos in chat needs the media server up. Text goes through; images do not travel between computers yet.
team.channelsNeedDeploy: Creating channels needs the updated server. Until then the team has a single conversation.
team.linkLocalOnly: Linked on this computer only: the server does not sync links yet.
team.mapUnknown: The app doesn't know which map this server runs yet. Open the server once to find out.
inv.help: This server's inventory. In Items you set how many of each item you have outside your bases (Shift + click adds 10). In Bases you draw each floor: square or triangular floors, walls with door, window, garage or custom (mod doors that span two wall slots), and place your crates, safes and lockers. Open a storage to put items in its grid, just like in the game. Each item's total is what's outside plus what's stored. Editor shortcuts: V move, P floor, T triangle (R rotates), W wall, B storage, E erase, Delete removes the selected storage.
inv.onbText: The inventory uses the game's own files and your Workshop mods: name, ID, icon, item size and the size of every crate, safe and locker.
inv.outsideHint: How many you have outside your bases
inv.whereEmpty: No storage holds this item. Open a crate in the Bases tab to store it.
inv.cat.title: Item catalog
inv.cat.summary: {items} items · {sources} source(s) · {icons} with game icon · {storages} storage types · read {when}
inv.cat.gameMissing: Not found — choose the Unturned folder
inv.cat.iconsHint: Icons: in game, open Workshop → F1 → "All Item Icons" to export them all to Extras/Icons, then read the catalog again. Without that, base-game items use an icon downloaded from the internet and mod items show an abbreviation.
inv.cat.notGame: That folder doesn't look like Unturned.
inv.scan.spawns: Working out where each item spawns…
inv.pdf.title: Export inventory (PDF in English)
inv.pdf.text: Every item with icon, quantity and the command to get it in game.
inv.pdf.loc: Include where each item is stored
inv.bases.confirmDel: Delete base "{name}" and everything recorded in it?
inv.bases.confirmDelStorage: Remove this storage and the {n} items stored in it?
inv.bases.needFloor: A base needs at least one floor.
inv.bases.emptyText: Draw each floor, the walls with doors and windows, and place your crates, safes and lockers where they are. Then open each one and organize the items like in the game.
inv.bases.hintSelect: Click a storage to select it and drag to move. Double-click opens it. Dragging empty space pans the view.
inv.bases.hintFloor: Drag to draw the floor on the grid. Near a triangle's slanted side, a click snaps a square onto it. Right button pans.
inv.bases.hintTri: Hover near any free side of another piece (even a triangle's slanted side) and click to snap a triangle there. Away from pieces it lands on the grid; R rotates.
inv.bases.hintWall: Click (or drag) near a tile edge to place the chosen wall type. The triangle's slanted sides work too.
inv.bases.hintStorage: Click the grid to place the chosen storage. On top of another, it stacks (up to 3).
inv.bases.hintStoragePick: Pick a storage from the list on the right.
inv.bases.hintErase: Click a wall to remove it; away from edges, erases the floor.
inv.bases.pickCustom: Create or choose a custom wall.
inv.bases.noSpanDiag: A multi-slot wall doesn't fit on a triangle's slanted side.
inv.bases.hint3d: Drag to orbit, right button pans, wheel zooms. Click a storage to open it.
inv.bases.resizeBlocked: A storage is outside that size; move it before shrinking.
inv.bases.noStorages: No storage found in the catalog.
inv.bases.selectHint: Select a storage on the grid to see what's inside.
inv.bases.clickMap: Click the map where the base is.
inv.bases.otherServer: This point is linked to a base on another server.
inv.bases.noLayout: This point has no base layout yet.
inv.walls.title: Custom walls
inv.walls.text: For mod doors and gates that take more than one wall slot. Each one belongs to this base.
inv.walls.confirmDel: Delete "{name}"? Walls of this type are removed from the base.
inv.walls.created: "{name}" created. Click an edge to place it.
inv.sm.searchHint: Search an item by name or ID to store it here.
inv.sm.handHint: Click a free slot to store it. R rotates, Esc drops.
inv.sm.idleHint: Pick an item on the left to store it, or click an item in the grid to edit it. Drag to move; right-click removes.
inv.sm.confirmClear: Take all {n} items out of this storage?
inv.bases.stackHint: Click the same spot again to cycle through.
inv.bases.stackFull: There are already {n} storages stacked here.
inv.bases.tObjectTitle: Claim flag, generator, sentry, bed, workbench, light… (O)
inv.bases.hintObject: Click to place the chosen object. Its action area shows around it (claim, generator, sentry, workbench…).
inv.bases.hintObjectPick: Pick an object in the Objects tab on the right.
inv.bases.objGroundFloor: {name} must touch the ground: ground floor only.
inv.bases.objGroundBuilt: {name} must touch the ground: place it off the built floor.
inv.bases.objTooClose: Too close to another object (the game needs clear space around it).
inv.bases.noObjectsCatalog: No objects in the catalog. Read the catalog again (Catalog → Read catalog) to load flags, generators, sentries and the rest.
inv.bases.claimNote: Dashed line: another group's claim flag can't be placed within 64 m.
inv.bases.groundNote: Must touch the terrain (oil-bearing ground) — in game it can't sit on floors/structures, only on the ground floor, off the built floor.
inv.bases.lightNote: ≈ light range is an estimate: it lives in the game's 3D model, not in the .dat files.
inv.mat.label: Material
